subject: FinCorp evals: next steps & dataset format
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Desai <samir@fincorp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: FinCorp evals: next steps & dataset format

Hi Samir / Elena —

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the time. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps to get a representative eval run up on Redwood: 

Recap / goals
- Primary objective: measure extraction accuracy and hallucination rate on FinCorp's transaction-routing assistant for high-value intents (chargeback, dispute, refund).
- Success criteria: critical intent exact-match >= 90% on auto-eval + sample human review pass rate >= 95% for escalations.

Recommended initial model line-up (we'll run comparisons):
- rw-instruct-16k-v1 (high-quality instruction model, 16k context)
- rw-chat-8k-quant (cost-optimized quantized chat model for throughput)
- rw-retrieval-8k (for runs with retrieval-enabled prompts)

What we need from FinCorp to run a customer-specific eval:
1) Dataset: CSV (or JSONL) with the following columns: id, prompt, expected_response, intent_label, metadata (optional). Example attached: fincorp_sample_dataset.csv
2) Size: start with 200–1,000 examples representative of production distribution (include both short and long contexts).
3) Scoring rules: provide a pass/fail mapping for critical intents and a free-text scoring rule for open responses (we'll compute BLEU/ROUGE-L plus a semantic similarity score).
4) Access: where to pull data (S3 path) or a Drive share; if data contains PII, please confirm redaction or provide a hashed/anonymized export.

Attachments: fincorp_sample_dataset.csv (sample rows), eval_instructions.md (format + scoring rubric), redwood-eval-template.jsonl (a template for running the eval on our console).

Proposed next steps
- You: share a 200–500 example sample set (or a link to S3/Drive) by EOD Monday so we can spin up the first run.
- Us: schedule a 30-min walkthrough of the eval template and map scoring criteria (I'll invite Neha).
- After the first run: we'll share per-intent metrics, regression flags, and recommended prompt/model adjustments.

Let me know if that works and if you have any constraints on sharing data. Happy to redact any fields or sign an NDA if needed.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Hi Samir — great questions, answers below.

On Fri, Mar 5, 2027 at 11:02 AM Samir Desai <samir@fincorp.com> wrote:
> 1) For expected_response: is free-text OK (we'll include the ideal phrasing), or do you prefer structured labels for the critical intents?

Either works — for critical intents we recommend providing both: a structured intent_label (e.g., CHARGEBACK, REFUND, DISPUTE) + an ideal free-text response where applicable. That lets us compute intent accuracy and also evaluate response quality.

> 2) For scoring: you mentioned semantic similarity. Can you share the threshold you use for pass/fail on open text?

Our default auto-eval thresholds (configurable per-run):
- Intent accuracy: exact match on normalized label (pass if >= 90%)
- Open-text: semantic similarity (embedding cosine) >= 0.82 for pass; additionally BLEU >= 0.35 OR ROUGE-L >= 0.40 as complementary signals.
- We always sample 5% of failed cases for human review to catch false negatives.

> 3) PII handling

If you can remove obvious PII (names, account numbers) that's ideal. If that's not possible, upload into an S3 bucket with the least-privilege IAM role and share a presigned URL or add redwood-eval@redwood.com with read-only access. We can also accept a hashed/anonymized export. We'll not persist sensitive fields beyond the eval run unless you opt in to retention.

Sandbox access: we can provide a read-only eval run URL + a short-lived API key for you to trigger runs in your staging account. If you'd rather have us run and share results, we can do that for the first two pilots.

I've attached the eval template (redwood-eval-template.jsonl) and the instructions doc (eval_instructions.md) which shows the exact column names and a sample scoring config.

Would you be free for a 30-min walkthrough on Monday 3/8 at 10:00 AM PT? I'll include Neha (our inference engineer) to go over the rubric.

Best,
Marissa
